script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. NEW YORK CITY - DAY

A bustling metropolis, filled with taxis honking, people talking, and the sound of sirens in the distance.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JESSICA (mid-20s, bookish, wearing glasses) sits at a table, typing away on her laptop. She's engrossed in her work, hardly noticing the commotion outside.

Suddenly, a FOLDABLE BIKE crashes into the shop, knocking over a display of mugs.

JOE (mid-20s, rugged, wearing a backpack) enters, looking flustered. He sets the bike down and rushes over to help Jessica.

JOE: (panicked) I'm so sorry! Is everyone okay?

Jessica looks up, surprised.

JESSICA: (shaking her head) It's just a few mugs. I'm fine.

JOE: (relieved) Thank goodness. That was close. I really need to be more careful.

Jessica smiles and sets her laptop aside.

JESSICA: Maybe you should take the bike outside and practice.

JOE: (grateful) I will. Thanks. I'm Joe, by the way.

Jessica: Jessica. Nice to meet you, Joe.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Jessica finishes her work and packs up her things. She sees Joe chatting with the barista.

Jessica approaches.

JESSICA: Hey, Joe. I'm heading out.

JOE: (surprised) Oh, hey Jessica. I didn't realize it was you.

They share a moment of awkward silence.

JESSICA: I guess I'll see you around.

JOE: (nodding) Sure. Have a good night.

Jessica leaves, feeling a pang of sadness.

INT. JOE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Joe sits on his couch, staring at his phone. He looks frustrated.

Suddenly, there's a knock on the door.

It's Jessica, holding a bag of takeout.

JESSICA: (smiling) I saw you sitting here looking sad. I thought I'd bring you some dinner.

JOE: (surprised) Really? That's nice of you.

They share a meal and conversation, laughing and getting to know each other.

INT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

Joe and Jessica sit on a bench, watching the world go by.

JESSICA: I'm glad we met, Joe. You've made my days a little brighter.

JOE: (looking at her sincerely) And yours have made mine. I'm really glad we're friends.

They share a moment, their hands brushing.

Jessica pulls away, looking embarrassed.

JESSICA: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to...

JOE: (smiling) It's okay. I felt it too.

They share a romantic kiss, their friendship blossoming into something more.

FADE OUT.

THE END
